verdict.rationale: Statsig documents official Client and Server SDKs, including a JavaScript SDK and a React StatsigProvider for web. It also documents deterministic evaluation that returns the same result across client and server platforms, which directly addresses consistent flag behavior across the stack. However, the evidence never names a specific mobile SDK (iOS/Android/React Native), so the mobile part of the story is only implied by mobile targeting. missing for 10: explicit documentation of official mobile SDKs, an enumerated list of supported backend languages, and independent hands-on corroboration of cross-platform consistency.

support.subject: As a developer, I can use official SDKs across my whole stack — backend, web, and mobile — with consistent flag behavior

citations.quote: Given the same user object and the same state of the experiment or feature gate, Statsig always returns the same result, even across different platforms (client or server).
Many customers deploy both Server and Client SDKs, which lets them gate features on both the client and server side.
After initialization, both Client and Server SDKs evaluate experiments/gates _without a network request_, and typically in less than 1ms.
